source_review.notes: Checked all seven structured references at their official vendor or project documentation URLs; each returned HTTP 200. Claims about BigQuery nested/repeated denormalization and repeated-query materialization, Snowflake column/micro-partition pruning, Redshift and PostgreSQL materialized-view persistence/refresh, and Iceberg stable field identity match the cited primary sources.

evidence: Checked definitions and uses of F, D, W, K, P, c_i, measure m, drift Delta, allocation weights, workload cost, and dependency watermarks.
Chapter validation accepted all GitHub-rendered display math and command syntax.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Symbols retain one meaning and formulas state whether they apply to left joins, additive measures, allocations, or empirical cost comparisons.

evidence: Recomputed the executable example: base revenue 100+80+120=300; functional enrichment keeps 3 rows and 300; two history matches for each c1 fact create 5 rows and 520.
Recomputed Exercise 2: left-join multiplicities 1+2+1+3=7, base sum 200, joined sum 390, and drift 190.
Checked Example 3: repeating 100 order shipping across four items gives 400, while equal allocation gives 25 per item and reconciles to 100.
numerical_recomputation.notes: All explicit counts, sums, multiplicities, allocation examples, and drift values reproduce.

evidence: Derived left-join measure total as sum_i m_i max(1,c_i) and drift as sum_i m_i(max(1,c_i)-1).
Confirmed the measure-preservation corollary from the one-to-one base-key mapping under c_i<=1.
Confirmed allocation reconciliation when nonnegative child weights sum to one.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The algebra consistently distinguishes zero-match null extension, one-match enrichment, positive fanout, and explicitly changed child grain.

evidence: Reviewed zero, one, and multiple dimension matches; overlapping Type 2 intervals; exact half-open interval boundaries; missing dimensions; multi-tenant natural keys; empty/null arrays; and signed-measure cancellation.
Reviewed parent-child and many-to-many fanout, current versus as-of changes, CDC deletes and join-key updates, partial publication, stale materializations, and restricted-column propagation.
Prerequisite fixture and ten examples cover duplicate keys, late dimensions, retroactive corrections, unused columns, benchmark cache state, and failed refreshes.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Boundary analysis separates grain-changing relationships from invalid fanout and requires key-set evidence even where totals accidentally cancel.

evidence: Checked exact base-key preservation, right-side match multiplicity, additive-measure preservation, nonoverlapping temporal intervals, child allocation reconciliation, and coherent publication versions.
Executable verification passed and detects both row-count and revenue drift in the nonunique history join.
Security and lifecycle invariants require materialized copies and old versions to retain access, deletion, and retention controls.
invariant_checking.notes: Each invariant names its grain, temporal scope, dependency version, or tolerance and avoids relying on one grand-total check.

evidence: Reviewed the row-preservation argument case by case: a left join emits one null-extended row for zero matches and one enriched row for exactly one match.
Verified the bijection conclusion under c_i<=1 and the additive-measure corollary when measures are copied unchanged over the same eligible base set.
Verified the fanout counterexample disproves preservation once a fact has two eligible matches.
proof_review.notes: The proof is valid under the complete join predicate and explicitly excludes filters, changed grain, allocations, and recomputed measures.

evidence: The formal claim is labeled row-preservation theorem and its consequence measure-preservation corollary, with assumptions immediately adjacent.
Storage and workload equations are presented as estimates/objectives rather than universal performance proofs.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: The chapter differentiates logical proof, counterexample, invariant, cost model, and workload-dependent empirical result.

evidence: The executable Python snippet demonstrates one finite cardinality error and does not claim database performance evidence.
The empirical evidence boundary limits benchmarks to the tested engine, data distribution, query mix, concurrency, cache state, and configuration.
The benchmark section requires p50/p95, scan, compute, storage, refresh, freshness, and recovery evidence rather than one runtime.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Performance recommendations remain conditional on representative measurement; the only universal claims are relational results under stated assumptions.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed wide table, bounded OBT, read model, flat/nested/aggregate/materialized shapes, grain, fanout, temporal attributes, columnar projection, freshness, incremental maintenance, semantic ownership, and lifecycle. The module treats denormalization as an intentional derived representation rather than a replacement for source truth.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed actionable design for cardinality matrices, many-to-one validation, Type 2 lookup, bridges/arrays/allocation, full and affected-key refresh, CDC, atomic publication, rollback, schema migration, access policy, query telemetry, workload benchmarking, and retirement. Failure fixtures cover common production defects.

pedagogical_review.notes: The one-page review frames the trade; exposition moves from purpose and grain through correctness, physical economics, operations and governance; notation supports the theorem and counterexample; ten distinct examples make failure modes concrete; and five exercises with complete answers cover design, arithmetic, benchmarking, maintenance and audit.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed. References and local execution were checked on 2026-09-02, but workload-specific database benchmarks, organization-specific privacy controls, and future engine behavior remain outside this review.
